result.summary:
Working tree vs. main (no commit yet on this branch, matching SECURITY-REVIEWER's own note) shows exactly three substantive files touched: apps/mobile/test/guards/v1_scope_boundary_guard_test.dart (new), docs/mobile/architecture.md (S4 replaced), docs/migration/stage-9-mobile.md (new section appended) -- confirmed via `git status --short` and `git diff` directly, not from MOBILE-DEV's or SECURITY-REVIEWER's summaries.

1. IDIOMATIC vs. CRUTCH.
This is pure Dart test code (two pure-function checkers + a real-tree wiring test + self-tests), matching the established shape of the other 7 files in apps/mobile/test/guards/ exactly: forbidden-list constants with inline reasoning comments, a Violation class with toString(), a pure checker function taking in-memory data so self-tests don't touch the filesystem, and a main() with the real-tree assertion first followed by self-tests -- same ordering convention as the precedent files. Checker A reuses the exact extractPubspecYamlDependencyNames/extractPubspecLockPackageNames logic from forbidden_dependencies_guard_test.dart, duplicated verbatim per the design doc's OQ-1 and consistent with the project's already-established precedent of duplicating _relativeTo/_readRealLibFiles-style helpers across guard files rather than sharing them. No crutch: nothing here is a GenServer standing in for a state machine (not applicable to Dart anyway) or a hand-rolled dispatch loop; it is a straightforward regex-based static lint, which is exactly what this class of guard is supposed to be, and the file's own doc comment is explicit that it is a textual heuristic, not an AST/type-level check -- same honesty standard as token_storage_boundary_guard_test.dart.

2. SUPERVISION / LIFECYCLE INTEGRITY. Not applicable -- no OTP, no gen_statem, no supervised process, no Riverpod provider lifecycle in this diff. This is file-system/text-scanning test code with no runtime state to isolate or leak. Noted explicitly rather than silently skipped.

3. TYPE-SAFETY GAPS. Checker B's key-weight map (_requestShapeKeyWeights) and violation classes are already typed (String/int fields, no stringly-typed ad hoc maps escaping the function boundary); nothing here represents a class of invalid state that a struct/enum change would make unrepresentable. Nothing filed under docs/issues/ from this diff.

4. SCOPE CREEP. `git status --short -- lib/letflow web` returns nothing for this diff's substantive changes (the only lib/letflow/ hit is the new design doc itself, which is documentation, not application code, and is explicitly the CODE-DESIGNER artifact for this very requirement). No lib/letflow/ backend code and no web/ file touched. Every piece of the new guard file traces to a BUILDS item in the design doc (Checker A = SS1.1, Checker B = SS1.2, self-test fixtures = SS1.3) and every piece of the design doc traces to REQ-430's own acceptance criteria (static guard + two docs edits). No new abstraction, behaviour, or generic plumbing introduced beyond what MOB-8's close-out needs -- this is the capstone requirement closing S9's scope, not opening new surface.

5. ANTI-PATTERNS / BUSYWORK CHECK. Checker B is not grep-a-keyword-and-declare-done: it requires 2-or-more distinct key-name tokens (weighted, with 'request' alone counting as 2) found as either a quoted map key or a disambiguated named-argument token (negative lookbehind excludes member-access collisions like `foo.method`), inside a bounded window around a `.record(...).put(` call-site -- this is real, if deliberately limited, shape detection, with two self-tests proving both a true positive (fixture (c), method/url/body map) and a true negative (fixture (d)-equivalent: a definition-cache-shaped put with unrelated keys 'definition_id'/'version'/'schema' producing zero violations) -- the negative fixture is exactly what distinguishes genuine shape detection from keyword-matching busywork, since a naive keyword grep would have no concept of a non-matching control case to prove against. Checker A's self-tests (firebase_messaging, workmanager) likewise prove real forbidden-list matching, not a vacuous assertion. Followed faithfully: same Violation-class/pure-function/self-test-fixture shape as both forbidden_dependencies_guard_test.dart (Checker A's direct precedent) and token_storage_boundary_guard_test.dart (Checker B's direct precedent, including that file's same up-front honesty framing of what the heuristic does and does not catch).

6. CHECKER B'S WINDOW-SHAPE DEVIATION (design OQ-2). Read the actual implementation rather than trusting the MOBILE-DEV handoff's characterization. The design's own OQ-2 offered two options: a true smallest-enclosing-block scan, or 'a fixed window of the preceding 400 characters plus the statement itself.' MOBILE-DEV implemented neither literally -- it is a symmetric fixed window, 400 chars before match.start AND 400 chars after match.end. On inspection this is not merely acceptable but closer to necessary: the regex `\.record\([^)]*\)\.put\(` matches up to and including the `.put(` call's own open paren, so the map-literal argument -- `{...}`, the entire thing Checker B exists to inspect -- begins immediately AFTER match.end, not before it. A preceding-only window as OQ-2's literal first phrasing describes would miss the common case entirely (including the design's own fixture (c), which places the map directly as the .put() argument). The design doc's own parenthetical ('plus the statement itself') already anticipated needing forward reach to the statement's end; MOBILE-DEV's fixed symmetric window is a simpler, regex-safe way to get that same forward reach without parsing to a terminating semicolon (which a naive scan risks desyncing on, same caveat the design doc raised for brace-counting). Verified empirically: the shipped self-tests for fixture (c) (method/url/body, true positive) and the negative fixture (definition-shaped put, true negative) both pass against this exact window implementation (read directly, not re-run -- TEST-RUNNER's own pending run will confirm `flutter test` result). This is a reasonable, in-file-documented implementation choice (the file's own doc comment on _scanWindowChars states the choice and its accepted false-negative boundary explicitly), not a crutch, and does not affect AC1's required-fail fixtures per the design doc's own OQ-2 analysis. Non-blocking.

7. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY. Checked docs/migration/decisions/0020-frontend-architecture.md's D1a clause directly (grepped and read in context via docs/mobile/requirements.md's citations, since 0020 itself states D1a's content by reference to the same text). architecture.md's new closing paragraph ('Offline form population is in; offline submission is out') is a precise restatement of D1a's actual effect -- on-device Letflow.Engine.Expr evaluation for computed/visible_when/cross-field-validation (interactivity only, server re-evaluates on submit) without any write-queue or conflict model -- and does not relax, contradict, or quietly re-decide D1a; it reinforces the same boundary with a new static guard. No contradiction found. Also checked docs/mobile/{README.md,architecture.md,requirements.md,build-order.md} and 0012-mobile-tier-stack.md for any other tension -- none; no new pubspec dependency, no general scripting runtime, no offline-write cache introduced by this diff (Checker A/B's entire purpose is to statically forbid exactly those things going forward).

8. DOCS SPOT-CHECK. Verified several of the architecture.md scope-table's REQ-id mappings against docs/requirements.yaml directly: REQ-294 (Dart Expr evaluator, 0020 D1a step 12, S9) matches its 'MOB-1/Dart evaluator' table citation; REQ-423 (MOB-3 part 1, cache+delta sync) and REQ-425 (MOB-6, single API client) both match their table rows exactly, including status: done; REQ-385 ('no code change needed... REQ-126 frozen-at-creation') matches the table's 'noted here as context, not a delivering REQ' framing. Verified all five spot-checked test-file paths cited in stage-9-mobile.md's new phase-gate table exist on disk (apps/mobile/test/auth/authenticate_with_tenant_test.dart, .../renderers/renderer_state_view_ac2_backpressure_countdown_test.dart, .../guards/ios_ats_guard_test.dart, .../renderers/task/task_claim_conflict_test.dart, .../definitions/pinned_form_resolver_test.dart), and confirmed `ls apps/mobile/test/guards/` shows v1_scope_boundary_guard_test.dart alongside all 7 precedent guard files, matching both tables' citations of it.

No BLOCKER, no MINOR rework required. One non-blocking observation recorded above (Checker B's window-shape deviation from OQ-2's literal phrasing is not just acceptable but arguably corrects an underspecified premise in the design doc itself -- worth folding back into the design-doc-writing convention: a future OQ about a scan window should state which side of the call-site the value actually appears on before offering a preceding-only option as if it were viable).
